A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, four figures, Table 1 and appendices are available and readable, supporting reliable comparison despite substantial theoretical revisions and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic latent-recovery experiments and LLM representation analyses in Section 5 and Appendix I, with outcomes in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: V2 retains original synthetic experiments and analyses of Pythia, Llama and DeepSeek representations in Section 5 and Appendix H, including Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: V2 Section 2 explicitly specifies a deterministic generative mapping (x,y)=g(c), whereas v1 gives only the probabilistic factorization. This limits the formal model specification; the latent graph, discrete variables, prediction objective and implemented learning procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic DAG data and 27 semantic, morphological and multilingual concept categories listed in Table 1. The Llama-3 and DeepSeek-R1 evaluations already appear in v1 Appendix I, corresponding to v2 Appendix H.

E2.justification: Figures 3–4 retain the same evaluated Pythia, Llama-2, Llama-3 and DeepSeek-R1 variants. Neither version introduces or removes a competing algorithm from the empirical comparisons; cited identifiability approaches remain theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix G and v2 Appendix F retain the same masking procedure, simulation controls, variable-count ranges, MLP configuration, optimizer, linear probes and matrix normalization. Table 1 preserves all pair counts, and Figures 3–4 preserve the evaluated model sizes.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains both sensitivity analyses: varying observed-variable count to investigate invertibility, and varying ER graph structure and latent-variable count to investigate recovery robustness. No additional ablation, robustness test or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both experimental appendices specify five simulation runs with different random seeds. Figure 2 retains the same mean and standard-deviation reporting, with no added uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: The underlying plots in Figures 2–4 are identical across versions, including simulation accuracies and every LLM matrix-product heatmap. Their accompanying empirical findings are retained; the appendix results are relocated, not newly added.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Definition 2.1 using epsilon=1−p(c*|x,y), and replaces the Jensen-based approximation and Jensen-gap appendix with an explicit residual decomposition and exact/asymptotic recovery arguments. Corollary 4.1 changes from a single-column direction to a weighted difference of two configuration columns under an additional concentration condition. Corollary 4.2 changes WA=I to WA≈I, with corresponding revisions to Appendices C–E.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain their broad claims about concept recovery and unifying linear representations. However, the introductory Figure 1 now asserts an o(epsilon) error term instead of v1's unquantified affine approximation, strengthening the stated precision of the central claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 revises the explanation of concept directions and steering from one column of A to weighted differences between two latent-configuration columns. Section 5 correspondingly describes As as part of a variant of A. The dedicated limitations and world-model discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details are retained through Appendix G becoming Appendix F: three 256-unit MLP layers, batch normalization and ReLU, Adam at 1e-4, scikit-learn LogisticRegression and matrix normalization. No new hardware, training-time or code/data access information appears.

R1.justification: Removal of the Jensen-gap discussion also removes the references to Gao et al. (2017) and Simic (2008, 2009). The substantive positioning against prior linear-representation and causal-identifiability research remains essentially unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

P1.justification: The principal narrative and section sequence are retained. Local restructuring removes Section 3's subsection split and proof sketch, revises theoretical explanations, retitles Section 4.2 and updates the appendix organization. The generic Impact Statement is removed, while most introductory, experimental and concluding prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text and references from two columns to one, removes running headers, redraws Figure 1 with the epsilon definition and revised guarantee, and resizes or relocates the retained figures and table. This substantially changes the document's visual presentation while preserving the experimental plots.

improvement.justification: V2 makes residual terms and concentration assumptions more explicit than v1's Jensen approximation, but its revised proofs do not securely establish the stronger guarantees. Appendix C does not justify cancellation of the residual expectations, and Appendix D discards log o(epsilon) terms despite their divergence. With empirical evidence unchanged, the gains in explicitness coexist with unresolved proof problems, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
